questions.stem: An atom of phosphorus has an atomic number of 15 and a mass number of 31. How many neutrons does it contain?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 31 - 15 = 16. A common mistake is to confuse the atomic number with the mass number, or to add them instead of subtracting. The mass number counts all nucleons (protons + neutrons), so subtracting the protons gives the neutrons.

options.text: Because neutrons cancel out the charge of protons
Because the number of protons equals the number of electrons
Because the nucleus has no overall charge

questions.explanation: In a neutral atom, the number of protons (each with +1 charge) equals the number of electrons (each with -1 charge), so the charges cancel out to give zero overall charge. Neutrons have no charge so they do not affect electrical neutrality. The nucleus itself is positively charged due to protons.

questions.stem: A student says: 'Removing an electron from a sodium atom would halve its mass.' Why is this statement incorrect?

options.text: Because sodium atoms cannot lose electrons
Because electrons have negligible mass compared to protons and neutrons
Because removing an electron would also remove a proton
Because electrons and protons have the same mass

questions.explanation: Electrons have a mass of approximately 1/1836 of a proton, which is negligible. Almost all the mass of an atom is in the nucleus (protons and neutrons). Removing an electron would barely change the atom's mass at all, certainly not halve it. The atom would become a positive ion but retain virtually all its mass.

questions.stem: An atom has 26 protons and a mass number of 56. How many of each subatomic particle does it contain?
questions.explanation: Protons = 26 (given). Neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 56 - 26 = 30. Electrons = Protons = 26 (in a neutral atom). This is an iron atom (Fe). Option (a) incorrectly calculates neutrons as equal to protons, which is a common error.

questions.stem: Which subatomic particle determines how an element reacts chemically?
questions.explanation: Electrons, particularly those in the outermost shell, determine how an element reacts chemically. Chemical reactions involve the transfer or sharing of electrons between atoms. Protons define the element and neutrons affect the mass, but neither directly participates in chemical bonding.
